title: Design a Credit Card Application Page and Its Confirmation Page
description: Design a credit card application page and its confirmation page: one form store with layered validation, sensitive fields kept out of logs and storage, a submit that creates one application, and a confirmation that reads status.

seo.title: Credit Card Application Page Frontend System Design
seo.description: Design a credit card application page: one form store, sensitive fields kept out of logs, one application per submit, and a status-read confirmation.

premiumPreview.summary: Design a credit card application page and its confirmation page where one form store owns the fields, a retried submit creates one application, and a refresh never posts the form again.
learningOutcomes: Keep every field and its errors in one form store and validate in three layers.
Keep sensitive values out of logs, URLs, analytics and browser storage, and mask them on the confirmation.
Send each submit with an idempotency key and render all five outcomes.
Make the confirmation a status read, so a refresh or a second tab never resubmits.
premiumPreview.unlockDescription: Premium unlocks the worked example of a double click during a slow submit, the typed form and gateway contracts, the application API semantics and the failure playbook.

practice.candidatePrompt: Design the frontend of a credit card application page and the confirmation page after it. An applicant enters identity, address, income and housing costs, reviews the terms and submits. The decision can be approved, declined, pending review or a request to verify identity. Walk through the components, where form state and validation live, how sensitive fields are protected, and what the confirmation shows after a refresh.
constraints: Sensitive fields never reach logs, URLs or storage.
expectedDecisions: Keep every field in one form store, validate on blur, per section and on the server, and map the server's field errors back by name.
Send each submit with an idempotency key and give every outcome its own screen: approved, declined, pending review, verify identity and failure.
Replace the submit entry with a status route that reads the application by id and shows masked values, so a refresh reads instead of posting.

mustCover: One form store owns every field and its errors.
Each submit carries an idempotency key.
strongSignals: Sensitive values are masked and never logged.
The confirmation reads status, so a refresh never resubmits.
evaluationSpine.expertStretch: Resuming a draft on another device without sensitive fields.
evaluationSpine.redFlag: Refreshing the confirmation posts the form again.
